checks.comparison: Elaborated Hist.step T gamma k h reply sets nodes(k+1) := nodes(base k) - gamma • (if grad k = k then reply else replies(grad k)) and replies(k) := reply, leaving every other entry unchanged. Tree.realize starts from V = {x0} (nodes = const x0) and at step k feeds reply g(nodes(point k))(eta k). This is w^{k+1} = w_base - gamma grad f(w_grad; eta) with w_base = node base k, w_grad = node point k and eta = tape coordinate k ~ D_xi, plus storage of the computed gradient for reuse. birch runs the same recursion through the template: query = (oracle 0, nodes(point count)), update = Hist.step at count.

Nothing is added to Algorithm 1 beyond the accepted reuse interpretation (an edge weighted by the earlier computation grad k, which equals the current reply when grad k = k) and the fixed public tree. When the tree is WellFormed, the stored replies and node values agree with Tree.reply and Tree.vertex. For ill-formed trees the total definitions return defaults, and those trees are excluded by valid in the setup.

The Tree structure (base, point, grad : N -> N) records each step's choices. WellFormed: base j <= j, point j <= j, grad j <= j, so only already computed points and gradients are used. foldHist/fold implement recursion over the unique parent: fold (k+1) = step k (fold (base k)), because foldHist k j = fold j for j <= k (unchanged entries). The vertex set N with edges base j -> j+1 is the computation tree.
Each node j+1 has exactly one parent, base j < j+1, so the structure is a rooted tree at node 0 = w^0. Nothing else is added.

IsMainBranch m := m 0 = 0 and, for all k, 0 < m(k+1) with base(m(k+1) - 1) = m k: node m(k+1) is created from node m k, a direct successor. auxSample m k = grad(m(k+1) - 1) is the computation whose gradient weights that edge, so xi^k = eta(auxSample). auxNode = point(auxSample) is z^k. Hence x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g(z^k; xi^k) by Hist.step.
The strict-positivity conjunct only rules out the degenerate m(k+1) = 0 (no edge into the root). No other condition is added.

depth 0 = 0 and depth(k+1) = depth(base k) + 1. ancestors 0 = {0} and ancestors(k+1) = insert (k+1) (ancestors(base k)), i.e. the root path including the node itself. dist y z = max(depth y - s, depth z - s) with s = sup of depth over ancestors y ∩ ancestors z. Ancestor sets are chains containing 0, so s is the depth of the closest common ancestor, and dist is the maximum number of edges to it (Def. 2.2). The example dist(w^9, w^4) = 4 is reproduced.
Natural subtraction never truncates, since s <= depth of both nodes. Nodes are their own ancestors, as accepted. No addition.

repr 0 = 0 (the empty multiset) and repr(k+1) = grad k ::m repr(base k): the multiset of computation indices applied along the root path. This matches Def. 2.3 under the accepted identification of a stochastic gradient by its computation. Multiplicities are preserved (Multiset, not Finset).
Nothing beyond the accepted interpretation.

gradientOracle P g is an Oracle (Point d) (Point d) with Seed k = Omega, law P on N -> Omega, and answer k q seed = g q.2 seed. Call k therefore returns grad f(x; xi) at the query point with the k-th tape sample, which is stochastic-gradient access over R^d = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d).
Only g values are revealed. f, the sample law and the lower bound are not inputs of this oracle or of birch.
EpsStationary f x P eps := Integrable (||gradient f (x omega)||^2) P ∧ integral of ||gradient f (x omega)||^2 dP <= eps. This is E||grad f(xbar)||^2 <= eps with eps on the squared scale.
Integrability is the accepted regularity, which keeps the totalized integral from making the inequality vacuous. Nothing else is added.

Public.gamma is any real, and the setup supplies stepSize > 0. Tree indices are N. Positivity domains (L > 0, eps > 0, ...) belong to the setup valid predicate, not to this unit. Definitions are total.

birch uses p.tree, p.gamma, p.x0, p.branch and p.K consistently. The call counter of the template, the State.count, the Hist.step index and the tape index of gradientOracle are the same k, so the reply for call k uses tape k, exactly as in Tree.realize.
The Prop definitions IsMainBranch and WellFormed are plain conjunctions and universal statements with the source polarity. No claim is hidden in a definition.
This unit states no source assumptions (A1-A3, C1-C3 belong to the setup). WellFormed and IsMainBranch are definitions used by valid.

stepSize L sigma eps R = min(1/(2L), min(if R = 0 then 1/(2L) else 1/(2RL), if sigma = 0 then 1/(2L) else eps/(4 sigma^2 L))). This equals the source min with omitted (+infinity) terms. horizon = ceil(4(R+1)L Delta/eps + 8 sigma^2 L Delta/eps^2) is the planned tuning, and both match the plan design text.

birch has: Seed Fin(K+1); initial state (count 0, nodes const x0, replies 0, chosen = seed); query (0, nodes(point count)); update (count+1, Hist.step at count); output nodes(branch chosen). This is the planned design and Algorithm 1 on the supplied tree, with the output selection memory in State.

The algorithm seed law is (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (K+1))).toMeasure on the measurable space Fin.instMeasurableSpace (elaborated record, hash verified). Its probability-measure proof is birch._proof_2. The oracle law is the supplied P on N -> Omega with the pi sigma-algebra. The template product law therefore makes the index independent of the tape, as planned.
This unit owns no convergence claim. It owns only definitions for PROB, ALG, TREE, DBRANCH, DDIST and DREPR.
Multiset repr and Finset ancestors are the planned representations.

Providers are Mathlib/LongTails basics: Rennala.Point = EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), PMF.uniformOfFintype, Multiset/Finset operations, Nat.ceil, Classical decidability for the real if-tests, and OracleTemplate.Algorithm/Oracle. No provider changes the meaning. I verified the SHA-256 of all 269 referenced records against their canonical JSON (0 mismatches). The axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Interfaces needed downstream exist with the planned types: Public(d, gamma, x0, tree, branch, K), birch : Public -> Algorithm (Point d) (Point d) (Point d) with numOracles 1, gradientOracle P g : Oracle (Point d) (Point d) 1, and Tree.vertex/reply/auxSample/auxNode for the setup and proofs.

R = 0 and sigma = 0 are handled by if-branches. horizon may be 0, and then Seed = Fin 1 is nonempty (birch._proof_1). Out-of-range or ill-formed indices give total default values that are irrelevant under WellFormed.

PROB maps to EpsStationary (eps-stationarity) and gradientOracle (stochastic-gradient access), both faithful as above.
ALG maps to the history and step, the realised run, the tuned step size and horizon, and the template algorithm birch. Together these implement Algorithm 1 on a fixed tree with the source step.
TREE maps to the tree structure, well-formedness and parent recursion.
DBRANCH maps to main branch and auxiliary sequence indices, matching Def. 2.1.
DDIST maps to the tree distance, matching Def. 2.2.
DREPR maps to the multiset representation, matching Def. 2.3.

notes: Definitions are total. For trees violating WellFormed they return defaults (unset nodes equal x0, unset replies equal 0), and foldHist reads stale entries. These cases are excluded by valid in the setup unit, which must include Tree.WellFormed as planned. Check this at setup review.
gradientOracle ignores the call index and the oracle ID in answer and uses only the tape coordinate. That is correct for a single oracle with call k reading tape k.
I used only packet evidence (source_code and declaration_evidence records, all 269 SHA-256 verified). The packet source equals the dev draft byte for byte, but the draft was not used as evidence.
